title: Record 85HA keyboard and N30 mouse qualification findings
body:
The owner's packaging identifies an 8BitDo N Edition keyboard (85HA) and N30 mouse (85CA). The earlier R8 research lead does not describe this mouse. This candidate records the actual hardware, cited per-control/per-connection capabilities, Windows/Wispr/Codex interfaces, mapping ownership and a reversible operator trial.

Refs #64. This is the source-evidence candidate; #64 remains incomplete and #65 remains blocked. The keyboard's genuine held output, N30 event identities/selective suppression, installed app versions and a complete supported route are unqualified. No input observer, mapping write, microphone use, app dispatch or installation ran. Read-only Windows inventory failed because this session could not execute Windows tools.

The canonical desktop-control document and generated guide incorporate the new evidence. Guide inputs reconcile concurrent #63 closure and merged source history. Public guide publication remains separate.

Validation on the committed candidate:

- Node 24: `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` passed; 11 specifications, 10 archives and 15 workflow tests. This documentation introduces no behavior or wire-contract delta, so no new OpenSpec capability is needed.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`: all five tests passed.
- `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`: coverage, links, navigation, interactions and print restoration passed at six widths. Desktop/mobile/print renders were inspected. The guide covers 95 open issues, 130 linked issues, 52 roadmap nodes and nine diagrams.
- All nine Archify artifacts passed 9/9 deterministic checks; guide regeneration produced no drift. The standalone desktop-input viewer still fails its viewport check for vertical overflow, with identical dimensions and diagnostics to the previous artifact. This existing limitation is retained, not reported as a pass.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews, including Windows/input compatibility, and all six applicable hosted jobs are pending. Merge eligibility depends on their results and the missing qualification evidence; this PR has no automatic issue-closure keyword. Source work does not establish installed, application or physical acceptance.

title: Reconcile desktop-control documentation completion in the guide
body:
Refs #63. Completion follow-up to #140.

PR #140 delivered the desktop-control documentation as `0d1b0930efae23912b942f6e65560763402fe665`. Independent Standards and Specification reviews and all six PR/main jobs passed; issue #63 is closed as completed. Guide issue #35 links the delivered document and marks only that checklist item complete.

Refresh the maintained guide to those verified facts. Retain closed #63 as a reference, remove it from primary open-issue coverage and the remaining-work roadmap, and refresh paginated repository history. The independent qualification path and all downstream preset gates are preserved. No product behavior, OpenSpec capability, architecture viewer or source pin changes.

The first pre-merge guard stopped when concurrent PR #135 advanced main. Merge that reviewed source revision intact and regenerate from a complete refresh. The snapshot now also records #30 closed after all six merged-main jobs passed; reconcile its guide status, coverage and remaining-work timeline without changing its tracker or product scope.

Validation at head `01035729b2f91db06db9e4a9afaeeedf85e9322b`, base/merge-base `8411413fa43329dba6e25acc4cb715ffbba7887f`:

- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py` passed: 94 primary open issues, 12 guides, nine unchanged viewers, 52 roadmap nodes and 109 merged PRs.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py` passed all five tests.
- `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs` passed with Node 24.21.0 and installed Playwright/Chromium: six widths, coverage/links, search/navigation, diagram inspection and print expansion/restoration. No page errors or main-page external requests.
- Rebuilding after commit produced no output drift; `git diff --check` passed. Guide SHA-256 `1271a0933a526b7d6affbe8e846890b5178efb1aef9c69c42bbfae700cc234ca`.

All 12 changed paths are under `docs/work-guide/`. Both workflows at the candidate revision exclude precisely that directory for pull requests and pushes to main. Current-head readbacks show zero runs/checks/statuses, no published reviews or unresolved threads, and MERGEABLE/CLEAN state, consistent with the existing SDLC guide-only CI exception. Protection/ruleset reads return the private-plan HTTP 403 and are recorded; no settings are changed. Renewed independent Standards/Specification reviews and final pre-merge/merged-main readbacks remain required. The guide uses the existing UI-approval exemption.

Public publication remains separate. The public landing page still serves hash `4d8f172a5025252c7b06551dfa862d1abe697fc532a54f75151d231217ed799e`; this PR does not publish it. No installation, hardware/input, application, transport or visible-device acceptance is claimed.

Delivery strategy: coordinator-owned guide edits and two independent reviewers, reusing the Standards and Specification contexts requested at gpt-5.6-terra/high. Three distinct agents used; no implementation workers or advisor consultations. Runtime settings/usage remain unexposed. Source review round 1 passed without corrections; guide review round 1 passed without findings but was superseded by the concurrent base change. Guide review round 2 is in progress at the fixed comparison above; no worker corrections, effort increases or promotions.

title: Verify bounded standalone cross-device compatibility
body:
Refs #9.

The reduced personal-project scope needs one compatibility check across the standalone Hub, actual dashboard, Pixoo and Nanoleaf. This adds a bounded synthetic runner using pinned owning source, disposable Linux state and fake physical boundaries. Twelve scenarios cover everyday Codex states, two same-project sessions, one Claude smoke, label/monitor acknowledgment, frontend Nanoleaf settings, MCP Pixoo mode, duplicate/late events, a disconnected consumer and restart without obsolete replay.

The existing product and UI code are unchanged. The runner checks native queued/applied receipts, current consumer connections, matching freshness and preserved effect epochs. Failed development attempts are recorded in `docs/cross-device-compatibility.md`; the report refuses overwrites and retains preflight failures. The runner rebuilds both TypeScript sources before importing output and forcibly reaps owned process groups when graceful shutdown fails. Both negative checks run in the required Hub CI suite. It reuses existing detailed contract, MCP and migration tests.

Local validation: Node 24.21.0/Python 3.14.4; 12 source scenarios with cleanup; build/type; 69 Hub tests; 5 dashboard tests and browser/matrix checks; TypeScript/Python controller/lifecycle/state suites; MCP/protocol; packaged Hub; 15 workflow tests; OpenSpec strict validation; guide generation, 5 maintenance tests and browser/print checks. Ten existing specification capabilities remain unchanged; this verification-only change explicitly uses `skip_specs: true`.

Guide inputs and HTML reflect #9's reduced scope and in-progress state. HTML SHA-256: `16b813fe25e7c75307f7faf23cf8056219a2718e45eee7ed63169b0351e705af`. Diagram ownership/flows are unchanged. Public publication is outside scope.

Draft while #30's report in PR #135 awaits delivery. The performance report used its own recorded runtime/pins; it is not relabeled as a timing measurement of #9's settings-capable Nanoleaf revision. Three independent Standards/Specification review rounds resolved all code findings through two correction batches. Final acceptance review after incorporating #30, OpenSpec archive, guarded merge remain pending. All six hosted jobs passed at `48b41a80ebc3fd03ff11206f8bfe10a03a939f00`. No installation, actual agent client, live migration or physical operation occurred.
